cases.query: Our company purchased a private motor car within the blocked input tax category and no exception applies. Does business use alone allow recovery of the GST?
cases.messageText:
# Answer

Regulations 26 and 27 generally disallow input tax on specified expenses, subject to the scope limits and exceptions in the regulations and IRAS guidance, and business purpose alone does not make a blocked claim recoverable. [IRAS: GST (General) Regulations](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-(gst)/claiming-gst-(input-tax)/conditions-for-claiming-input-tax)

Because your company purchased a private motor car within the blocked input tax category and no exception applies, business use alone does not allow recovery of the GST. [IRAS: GST (General) Regulations](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-(gst)/claiming-gst-(input-tax)/conditions-for-claiming-input-tax)

cases.query: We employ a covered employee in Singapore. Who is responsible for paying the monthly CPF contribution to the Fund: the employer or the employee?
cases.messageText:
# Answer

Every employer of an employee is responsible for paying monthly to the Fund in respect of each employee contributions at the respective rates prescribed in the First Schedule.

Because you employ a covered employee in Singapore, the employer is responsible for paying the monthly CPF contribution to the Fund.

cases.query: Our Singapore company plans to start regulated fund management. What should it establish about licensing or exemptions before commencing?
cases.messageText:
# Answer

A person carrying on a regulated activity in Singapore must assess whether a Capital Markets Services licence, registration, or a statutory or MAS exemption applies before conducting fund management.

Before commencing regulated fund management, your Singapore company must establish whether a Capital Markets Services licence, registration, or a statutory or MAS exemption applies to its planned activities.
